note: For each domain: the eight steps of the workflow and the performed/owned conditions for the eight judgment axes. The items, the result report and the experience input all read this one file. ME_V3_2 revised five domains. Actuation, transmission and motion design had read like control testing from electrical engineering, so it was moved toward load, inertia and drivetrains; materials was renamed to include strength; and for equipment and facility operation, requirements, constraints and schedule, and task automation, wording that only people with factory experience could answer was brought down to situations that can also be answered from undergraduate labs and capstone projects.

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A new product or a change request comes in as a specification or a preliminary review

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Required performance, space constraints, load conditions, cost targets and the production method

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: How many concepts to develop and which requirement to protect first

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Concept design, load path review, fastener and bearing selection, tolerance allocation, manufacturability review

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: 3D CAD, design calculations, tolerance stack-up calculations, standard part selection charts

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: Assembly and part drawings, BOM, design calculations, change history

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Comparison between designs, interference and tolerance stack-up, prototype assembly, analysis results, standards

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When there is interference, a part that cannot be assembled, or a breakage, narrow the cause down to dimensions, material or process

J1.l2: Wrote the design scope from a given specification
J1.l3: Set the functions and constraints to meet when no specification existed

J2.l2: Turned requirements into dimensions, loads, service life and assembly conditions

J3.l2: Decided one of thickness, cross-section, material or fastening
J3.l3: Set tolerance allocation and safety margins based on function

J4.l2: Built the geometry and assembly in 3D CAD
J4.l3: Documented clamping force, bearing life and stiffness with hand calculations

J5.l3: The drawings went to manufacturing, with the BOM and tolerances stated

J6.l2: Compared two or more designs against the same criteria
J6.l3: Checked interference and tolerance stack-up, or confirmed with a prototype

J7.l2: Ran into interference or a breakage and changed the dimensions
J7.l3: Narrowed the cause down to dimensions, material or process and prevented it from recurring

J8.l2: Presented it at a design review
J8.l3: Manufacturing or ordering went ahead based on that drawing

org_outcomes.OC1: Product performance, cost and assembly hours
org_outcomes.OC2: Meeting customer specifications and unit price
org_outcomes.OC3: Design deliverables on time and customer approval
org_outcomes.OC4: Device design as a project deliverable
org_outcomes.OC5: Experimental setup and the methods section of a paper
org_outcomes.OC6: A design that complies with standards, and the basis for it
org_outcomes.OC7: A working prototype and the launch schedule

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A request comes in to confirm whether a design will hold up under its load conditions

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Geometry model, material, load history, required life and allowable stress

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Which phenomenon to look at and how far to idealize

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Idealization, setting boundary conditions, checking mesh convergence, fatigue life calculation, sensitivity

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Finite element analysis, fatigue analysis, hand calculations, optimization, scripts

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: Analysis report, model files, predicted life, design change proposal

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Hand calculations, earlier analyses, test results, allowable values in standards, other analysts

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When results disagree with tests, narrow the cause down to boundary conditions, material or mesh

J1.l2: Decided which load cases to examine
J1.l3: Identified the governing phenomenon among fatigue, buckling and impact and set the scope

J2.l2: Turned the required life and allowable stress into analysis input conditions
J2.l3: Turned test standards or customer specifications into analysis conditions as well

J3.l2: Set the boundary conditions and loads
J3.l3: Chose the level of idealization and the material model

J4.l2: Built and ran a model in a commercial analysis tool

J5.l3: The report states the predicted life, assumptions and limitations

J6.l2: Compared with hand calculations or earlier results
J6.l3: Checked against test results and calibrated the model

J7.l2: Corrected the model when results disagreed with tests
J7.l3: Narrowed the disagreement down to boundary conditions, material or mesh

J8.l2: Reported the results to the design team
J8.l3: Drawing dimensions or materials changed as a result

org_outcomes.OC1: Fewer prototypes and a basis for design changes
org_outcomes.OC2: Passing customer validation and proving the specification
org_outcomes.OC3: Analysis reports used in customer decisions
org_outcomes.OC4: Technical basis for the project's interim review
org_outcomes.OC5: A paper with a validated model
org_outcomes.OC6: A traceable basis for judging compliance with standards
org_outcomes.OC7: A prototype that does not break, and lower material cost

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A problem of high temperature or insufficient flow comes up from testing or the field

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Heat generation, allowable temperature, flow rate, pressure drop target and operating environment

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: The dominant heat transfer path and which operating point to use as the design point

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Heat load calculation, thermal network setup, flow analysis, operating point selection, mesh independence check

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: CFD, thermal network calculations, 1D system analysis, processing measured data

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: Thermal design specification, analysis report, flow path design, basis for fan and pump selection

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: 1D calculations, literature values, measured temperatures and flow rates, earlier models

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When temperatures are higher than expected, narrow it down to the flow path, contact thermal resistance or fan selection

J1.l2: Decided whether the problem was the heat load or the flow rate
J1.l3: Identified the dominant path among conduction, convection and radiation and set the scope

J2.l2: Turned allowable temperature and pressure drop targets into boundary condition values
J2.l3: Included the operating environment and worst-case conditions in the conditions

J3.l2: Set the boundary conditions and operating point
J3.l3: Chose the turbulence model, meshing strategy and treatment of contact thermal resistance

J4.l2: Produced values with CFD or a thermal network calculation
J4.l3: Documented mesh independence and convergence criteria

J5.l2: Delivered an analysis report or a thermal design specification
J5.l3: The specification states the operating point, margins and assumptions

J6.l2: Compared with 1D calculations or literature values
J6.l3: Checked against measured temperatures and flow rates

J7.l2: Revised the design because temperatures were higher than expected
J7.l3: Narrowed the cause down to the flow path, contact or fan selection

J8.l2: Presented the results at a design review
J8.l3: The cooling structure or fan specification was decided from those results

org_outcomes.OC1: Product cooling performance and power consumption
org_outcomes.OC3: Thermal analysis reports on time and repeat requests
org_outcomes.OC4: Energy performance metrics for the project
org_outcomes.OC5: A paper with a validated heat transfer model
org_outcomes.OC7: A prototype that runs without overheating

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Reports that noise or vibration exceeds the standard come from testing or customers

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Target noise and vibration levels, excitation sources, structural model and operating conditions

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Which frequency band to look at, measurement points and excitation conditions

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Modal analysis, vibration measurement, frequency response analysis, transfer path analysis, verifying countermeasures

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Accelerometers and microphones, signal analysis, modal analysis, multibody dynamics

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: Measurement and analysis reports, countermeasure proposals, before-and-after tables, judgment of whether targets were met

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Analysis vs. measured modes, before and after countermeasures, target criteria, competitor products

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When a countermeasure has no effect, narrow it down to resonance, the excitation source or the transfer path

J1.l2: Decided which frequency band the problem was in
J1.l3: Identified whether structure-borne or airborne transmission was dominant

J2.l2: Turned allowable vibration and noise levels into measurement points and operating conditions
J2.l3: Turned ride comfort or quietness into measurable values

J3.l2: Set the measurement points and excitation conditions
J3.l3: Set damping and coupling conditions and chose the direction of the countermeasure

J4.l2: Carried out a modal analysis or vibration measurement
J4.l3: Used frequency response, order analysis and transfer path analysis

J5.l2: Delivered a measurement or analysis report
J5.l3: The report states the before-and-after comparison for the countermeasure and whether the target was met

J6.l2: Compared analysis modes with measured modes
J6.l3: Measured before and after the countermeasure under the same conditions

J7.l2: Took another look when a countermeasure had no effect
J7.l3: Narrowed the cause down to resonance, the excitation source or the transfer path

J8.l2: Reported the results to design or production
J8.l3: The structure, mounts or sound insulation specification changed as a result

org_outcomes.OC1: Quietness metrics and fewer customer complaints
org_outcomes.OC3: Root cause reports and repeat requests
org_outcomes.OC5: A paper with a transfer path model
org_outcomes.OC7: A prototype that runs without shaking

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: A requirement comes in for what has to move, how fast and how precisely

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Mass and inertia to be moved, required speed and acceleration, positioning accuracy, friction and resistance, available space

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Drive type, motor size, gear ratio, transmission type and how it stops

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Load torque calculation, reflected inertia, motion profiles, actuator selection, commissioning and tuning

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Drive sizing calculations, gearbox and transmission component data, motion profiles, response measurement, safety review

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: A moving mechanism or device, drive selection rationale, motion sequence chart, commissioning records

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Target cycle time, repeat positioning accuracy, motor margin, previous configuration

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When it is slow, vibrates or stops, narrow it down to inertia, friction, stiffness or gain

J1.l2: Separated what had to move from what would not move this time
J1.l3: Decided which required motions to give up and narrowed the scope

J2.l2: Turned required speed and positioning accuracy into numerical conditions
J2.l3: Fixed acceleration and margins as non-negotiable design conditions

J3.l2: Decided the motor size or gear ratio
J3.l3: Decided the drive type and transmission structure, and the build went ahead with that configuration

J4.l2: Calculated and checked load torque and reflected inertia
J4.l3: Adjusted acceleration or gains based on measured response

J5.l2: Delivered a moving mechanism or drive sizing calculations
J5.l3: A motion sequence chart and commissioning records were both kept

J6.l2: Compared actual motion with the target cycle time
J6.l3: Measured repeat positioning accuracy several times and checked the spread

J7.l2: Fixed it when it vibrated or stopped
J7.l3: Narrowed the cause down to inertia, friction, stiffness or gain

J8.l2: Handed the device over for other people to use
J8.l3: The device was used for real work and cut the time it took

org_outcomes.OC1: Line takt time and equipment uptime
org_outcomes.OC2: Meeting equipment motion specifications and passing delivery inspection
org_outcomes.OC3: Building equipment on time and repeat requests
org_outcomes.OC4: A project prototype that delivers the required motion
org_outcomes.OC5: An experimental setup that reproduces the required trajectory
org_outcomes.OC6: Judging compliance of drive units with safety standards
org_outcomes.OC7: Working equipment that takes load off people's hands

review_perspectives.name: Narrowing down causes of vibration and stalls

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Fracture, wear or deformation comes up from the field or testing

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Fracture surface, usage history, load conditions, environment and material specification

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Candidate causes of damage to investigate, and which material to use at what strength

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Fractography, microstructure examination, composition analysis, mechanical testing, comparative material testing

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Microscopes and analytical equipment, hardness and tensile testing, heat treatment, friction and wear testing

workflow.name: Outputs delivered
workflow.detail: Analysis report, material specification, test report, countermeasure proposal

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Values in standards, literature values, other materials under the same conditions, usage history

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When the cause cannot be narrowed to one, rule out the candidates one at a time with evidence

J1.l2: Decided how to interpret the damage
J1.l3: Listed fatigue, corrosion, wear and creep as candidates and set the scope

J2.l2: Turned the operating environment and required life into material requirements
J2.l3: Set the criteria where strength, cost and machinability conflicted

J3.l2: Decided the material or heat treatment conditions
J3.l3: Changed the combination of material and treatment to balance strength and cost, and that option was used

J4.l2: Carried out mechanical testing or microstructure examination
J4.l3: Combined fractography and composition analysis to identify the mechanism

J5.l2: Delivered a test report or an analysis report
J5.l3: The material specification and the basis for the judgment were documented

J6.l2: Compared with values in standards or the literature
J6.l3: Ran comparative tests against other materials under the same conditions

J7.l2: Took another look at why it broke
J7.l3: Ruled out candidate mechanisms with evidence and narrowed it down to one

J8.l2: Reported the results to design or quality
J8.l3: Material or process standards changed as a result

org_outcomes.OC1: Fewer field failures and lower warranty costs
org_outcomes.OC2: Meeting material specifications and unit price
org_outcomes.OC3: Root cause reports and repeat requests
org_outcomes.OC5: A paper identifying a damage mechanism

workflow.name: How the problem arrives

review_note: `review_perspectives` is the list of perspectives received in the 2026-10-07 quality review. Each perspective records which axis receives it, and `v3:domains` counts whether that axis has at least two items to choose from. If only the list is kept, nobody will notice when the next person deletes an item.
